chain.label: Inadequate FAA oversight of Fresh Air's Part 125 operation
chain.trigger: multiple FAA inspectors failed to perform effective oversight of Fresh Air, possibly due to a belief that Part 125 operations merit less scrutiny

chain.label: Fresh Air's deficient maintenance recordkeeping and unverifiable airworthiness status
chain.trigger: the investigation was unable to locate current documentation related to the accident airplane's status, including AD and SB compliance, engine and propeller records

caused_by.evidence: the PMI should have discovered Fresh Air's critically deficient recordkeeping during the last documented aircraft records inspection, conducted 7 days before the accident

chain.label: Leak at the right augmentor/exhaust muffler junction
chain.trigger: a leak in the vicinity of the augmentor/muffler junction allowed the fire to exit the junction and damage portions of the right wing

caused_by.evidence: the mechanic noted that oil and fuel leaks at the augmentor/muffler junction do occur

chain.label: Takeoff conducted with the ADI and autofeather systems off, contrary to the AFM
chain.trigger: the flight crew likely did not use the ADI and autofeather systems during the takeoff

caused_by.evidence: because the POI had never directly observed Fresh Air's operation, he was unaware that the airplanes were being operated contrary to the limitations outlined in the FAA-approved AFM

chain.label: Airplane 6,610 lbs over the maximum allowable takeoff weight for a dry takeoff
chain.trigger: the accident airplane exceeded the maximum allowable takeoff weight of 40,900 lbs

caused_by.evidence: because neither system was used on the accident flight, the maximum allowable takeoff weight was 40,900 lbs

chain.label: Captain's acute sleep loss of 3 to 5 hours
chain.trigger: the captain was likely suffering from acute sleep loss at the time of the accident, which would have negatively affected his ability to guide the first officer

chain.label: First officer's limited recent Convair experience and documented training deficiencies; captain's currency unverified
chain.trigger: considering the first officer's limited recent experience in the Convair CV-440 and the performance deficiencies identified in his training and certification history, he was likely not capable of handling the emergency without help from the captain

caused_by.evidence: the POI should have discovered the recordkeeping discrepancies and instructed the operator to verify the captain's currency; however, he did not

chain.label: In-flight fire in the right augmentor shortly after takeoff
chain.trigger: the thermal damage to the airplane resulted from the ignition of a flammable liquid in one of the right augmentors

caused_by.evidence: oil or fuel leaks into the exhaust system are capable of igniting in the presence of the high heat within the augmentors and would have led to the exhaust fire

chain.label: Crew shut down the right engine in response to the suspected engine fire
chain.trigger: the right engine settings were generally consistent with the engine being shut down

caused_by.evidence: although the investigation was not able to determine why the crew chose to shut down the engine, they likely suspected an engine fire due to the smoke

chain.label: Crew feathered the left propeller while the shut-down right propeller remained unfeathered
chain.trigger: the left propeller was found feathered at impact, with the left engine settings consistent with the engine at takeoff or climb setting

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew likely intended to shut down the right engine by bringing the mixture control lever to the IDLE CUTOFF position and feathering the right propeller
because the autofeather system was not activated, the flight crew had to manually feather the propeller and likely manually selected the left propeller to feather

chain.label: Overweight airplane unable to sustain altitude on asymmetric power during the return
chain.trigger: the radar data then indicate a relatively steady decline in altitude until the final right turn to align with runway 28

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was above the maximum allowable takeoff weight, making it even more difficult for the flight crew to maintain altitude or airspeed when operating with one engine
other Convair pilots described the airplane as only holding altitude at best on a single engine and when heavily loaded
feathering the propeller on a failed engine decreases drag, assisting the flight crew with single-engine operation

chain.label: Captain allowed the inexperienced first officer to fly during the emergency while he worked the radios
chain.trigger: the investigation was unable to determine why the captain allowed the first officer to fly the airplane when faced with an emergency

caused_by.evidence: with a first officer who had relatively little recent time in the Convair as the PF, the need for the captain's clear, unimpeded leadership would have been critical
this sleep loss would have led to degraded decision-making, inadequate risk assessment, and reduced leadership

chain.label: Flight crew failed to monitor and maintain adequate airspeed in the descending right turn to runway 28
chain.trigger: the calculated airspeed continually dropped as the airplane reduced its bank angle to stop the turn and align with the runway

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was operating close to both stall and controllability limits when radar contact was lost

a flight crew applying effective crew resource management, adhering to their PF and PM duties, and properly using a checklist to handle the emergency should have been able to maintain positive control
stress can lead to a phenomenon known as 'tunnel vision,' or the narrowing of attention, in which basic information like airspeed can be overlooked

chain.label: Aerodynamic stall or loss of directional control below minimum control speed
chain.trigger: the airspeed of the airplane reduced to a point where the airplane either experienced an aerodynamic stall or it dropped below the minimum control speed during the right turn

caused_by.evidence: the failure to maintain airspeed resulted in either an aerodynamic stall or a loss of directional control

chain.label: Airplane struck trees and crashed into Laguna La Torrecilla
chain.trigger: the airplane struck trees with its right wingtip and crashed into the lagoon while traveling in a northerly direction

caused_by.evidence: radar contact was lost with the airplane at 100 ft as it continued the right turn; shortly thereafter, the airplane struck trees

chain.label: Both pilots killed and airplane destroyed
chain.trigger: The two pilots died, and the airplane was destroyed by impact forces

caused_by.evidence: the fuselage and wing sections were fragmented from impact with the water
